name: Chloris

project_scope.selection_mode: Three installed canonical species plus two approved source-pool comparison dependencies
project_scope.range_status: All three canonical cards currently RANGE_UNRESOLVED; do not count as confirmed target-zone natives

look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Photograph the WHOLE flowering head before collecting a mature spikelet. Ask whether the racemes form crowded tiers, widely separated tiers, or one terminal fan. Then use a hand lens to inspect the upper sterile lemma (hood shape), fertile lemma awn, and marginal hairs.
shared_genus_traits: Warm-season grasses with radiating fingerlike racemes carrying spikelets along one side; the windmill silhouette alone is not species-diagnostic.
Each spikelet has glumes and a fertile floret with one or more reduced sterile florets above it. The fertile and sterile lemmas may bear different awns.
For species-level ID, examine a mature head plus a detached spikelet under 10–20× magnification and use a millimeter scale.

quick_key.if: Several CLOSELY packed tiers of SHORT racemes, upper sterile lemma rounded and swollen like a hood, awns very short
Widely SEPARATED whorls of LONG racemes, often one upright terminal branch, both lemma awns comparatively long
Racemes chiefly one TERMINAL digitate fan; annual tuft and conspicuous long hairs on fertile lemma margins
Intermediate between hooded and tumble windmillgrass
quick_key.then: Consider Chloris ×subdolichostachya; source-pool comparison only, taxonomy/installer dependency

species_comparison_matrix.verticillata: Perennial, sometimes rooting at lower nodes
~10–16 racemes in separated whorls, often a terminal upright branch
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: ~4–20 racemes mainly in one terminal whorl

species_comparison_matrix.verticillata: Not conspicuously inflated into a round hood
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: Reduced sterile florets, not the cucullata hood
Do not key on length alone; examine fertile lemma hairs

species_comparison_matrix.cucullata: Not the conspicuous >1.5 mm fringe of virgata
species_comparison_matrix.verticillata: Not the conspicuous >1.5 mm fringe of virgata
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: Long apical marginal hairs, often >1.5 mm; important tie-breaker

cautions: Never identify by purple or straw-colored heads alone; age changes color.
Raceme length and awn lengths overlap, especially between C. verticillata and C. virgata; use whorl arrangement, basal crown, and fertile lemma hairs together.
C. ×subdolichostachya is reported as a naturally occurring C. cucullata × C. verticillata hybrid. Intermediate heads should remain unresolved pending diagnostic review.
C. andropogonoides is in the Master Plant Pool but is not among these three canonical cards; avoid implying this key covers every local Chloris.
Do not use Texas state nativity to convert project county-level RANGE_UNRESOLVED into PASS.

lookalikes.difference: Source-pool Chloris with slender spike arrangement; needs targeted diagnostic review before adding a fourth key branch.
Natural C. cucullata × C. verticillata hybrid; may combine intermediate raceme and spikelet characters. Do not force either parent.
Also digitate grass heads, but Cynodon spikelets and branch layout differ; inspect spikelet under hand lens.
Radiating thick comb-like spikes, distinct spikelet shape; inspect branch tips and spikelet arrangement.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.look_for: Same-scale heads with arrows showing crowded whorls, spaced whorls, or terminal fan.
10–20× mature spikelet with arrow on upper sterile lemma and 1 mm scale.
Separate arrows for each lemma and its awn; measure in mm.
Matched side-lit macros with arrow to hairs near fertile lemma apex.
Plant base and lower nodes showing annual crown versus perennial rooting habit.
Future verified intermediate hybrid spikelet and whole head; no generic substitution.

Approved source-pool records not among the three canonical manifest species; check taxonomy decisions and installation readiness. Do not install from this lane.
